  "evidence_ids": ["E1.1", "E2.1", "E3.1"],
  "reasons": [
    "Customer payments for delivered garments represent cash inflows from principal revenue-generating activities (operating activities).",
    "Proceeds from selling an old cutting machine represent cash inflows from the disposal of a fixed asset (investing activities)."
  ],
  "syllabus_chapter": "Cash Flow Statement",
  "syllabus_topic": "Classification of cash flows into operating, investing, and financing activities",
  "syllabus_entitlement": true,
  "presentation_ready": true,
  "question_type_match": true,
  "principle_applicability": "excerpt_required",
  "decisive_principle_in_excerpts": true,
  "answer_conditions": [
    {
      "condition": "Customer payment arises from the sale of goods (garments) in the normal course of business.",
      "status": "explicit",
      "alters_key_if_changed": true,
      "convention_evidence_ids": []
    },
    {
      "condition": "Cutting machine is a fixed asset of the garment manufacturer.",
      "status": "convention",
      "alters_key_if_changed": true,
      "convention_evidence_ids": ["E3.1"]
    }
  ],
  "option_challenges": [
    {
      "option": "A",
      "strongest_reading": "Old cutting machine sale is treated as an ordinary business recovery within regular operations.",
      "correct_under_reading": false,
      "reading_status": "contradicts_stem",
      "convention_evidence_ids": []
    },
    {
      "option": "C",
      "strongest_reading": "Customer payments are treated as capital receipts while selling an old machine is considered routine operating income.",
      "correct_under_reading": false,
      "reading_status": "contradicts_stem",
      "convention_evidence_ids": []
    },
    {
      "option": "D",
      "strongest_reading": "Both transactions are viewed as raising capital funds for the business enterprise.",
      "correct_under_reading": false,
      "reading_status": "contradicts_stem",
      "convention_evidence_ids": []
    }
  ],
  "blocking_defects": [],
  "style_notes": [],
  "cuet_fit": {
    "criteria": {
      "syllabus_objective": {
        "level": 3,
        "evidence": "Tests core syllabus objective of classifying business transactions into operating, investing, and financing activities."
      },
      "format_authenticity": {
        "level": 3,
        "evidence": "Matches standard CUET UG MCQ format with direct application to business scenarios."
      },
      "level_calibration": {
        "level": 3,
        "evidence": "Direct conceptual application fully aligned with standard Class XII NCERT Accountancy level."
      },
      "discrimination_value": {
        "level": 3,
        "evidence": "Discriminates between candidates who confuse operational turnover with asset disposal proceeds."
      }
    },
    "reasoning_steps": 2,
    "estimated_difficulty": "easy",
    "cognitive_level": "application",
    "exemplar_ids_compared": ["cuet2024-accountancy-bookA-q19", "cuet2024-accountancy-bookA-q21"]
  },
  "option_resolution": [
    {
      "option": "A",
      "status": "contradicted",
      "false_part": "Both are operating cash inflows",
      "premise_source": "excerpt",
      "evidence_id": "E3.1",
      "premise_quote": "Cash receipt from disposal of fixed assets including intangibles.",
      "reason": "Proceeds from disposing of a cutting machine are investing cash inflows, not operating."
    },
    {
      "option": "B",
      "status": "supported",
      "false_part": "",
      "premise_source": "excerpt",
      "evidence_id": "E1.1",
      "premise_quote": "sale of garments, etc. These are the principal revenue generating activities (or the main activities) of the enterprise",
      "reason": "Customer payment is operating and disposal of machinery is investing."
    },
    {
      "option": "C",
      "status": "contradicted",
      "false_part": "Customer payment is investing; machine-sale proceeds are operating",
      "premise_source": "excerpt",
      "evidence_id": "E2.1",
      "premise_quote": "cash receipts from sale of goods and the rendering of services.",
      "reason": "Customer receipts for goods are operating cash inflows, not investing."
    },
    {
      "option": "D",
      "status": "contradicted",
      "false_part": "Both are financing cash inflows",
      "premise_source": "excerpt",
      "evidence_id": "E4.1",
      "premise_quote": "financing activities relate to long-term funds or capital of an enterprise, e.g., cash proceeds from issue of equity shares, debentures, raising long-term bank loans",
      "reason": "Neither receipt relates to issuing equity/debt or raising capital loans."
    }
  ]
}
